name: Stone tools
desc: Knapped stone flakes and cores, the oldest known human technology.

name: Control of fire
wiki: Control of fire by early humans
desc: Keeping and later making fire for heat, light, cooking and protection.

name: Spear
desc: A pointed shaft used for hunting and fighting; among the earliest weapons.

name: Rope and cordage
desc: Twisted plant or animal fibers that bind, haul and lash.

name: Clothing
desc: Hides and later textiles worn for protection and warmth.

name: Sewing needle
desc: An eyed bone needle for stitching fitted garments.

name: Bow and arrow
desc: A spring weapon that stores energy in a bent stave to launch arrows.

name: Dugout canoe
desc: A boat hollowed from a single log; among the oldest watercraft found.

name: Animal domestication
desc: Breeding dogs, sheep, goats, cattle and horses under human control.

name: Agriculture
desc: Cultivation of domesticated crops, beginning the shift to settled life.

name: Pottery
desc: Clay vessels hardened by fire for cooking and storage.

name: Kiln
desc: An enclosed oven reaching temperatures high enough for ceramics and lime.

name: Weaving
desc: Interlacing threads at right angles to make cloth.

name: Mudbrick
desc: Sun-dried bricks of mud and straw, the material of the first towns.

name: Irrigation
desc: Channeling water to fields to grow crops in dry land.

name: Plough
desc: A draft-animal tool that turns soil for planting.

name: Wheel
desc: A disc rotating on an axle, used first for pottery and carts.

name: Potter's wheel
desc: A spinning turntable for shaping symmetric clay vessels.

name: Cart
desc: A wheeled vehicle pulled by draft animals.

name: Sail
desc: A cloth surface that harnesses wind to propel a boat.

name: Smelting
desc: Extracting metal from ore with heat and a reducing agent such as charcoal.

name: Bronze
desc: A hard copper-tin alloy that gave its name to an age.

name: Iron working
desc: Smelting and forging iron from its ores.

name: Blast furnace
desc: A tall furnace blown with air that produces liquid iron continuously.

name: Cast iron
desc: High-carbon iron melted and poured into molds.

name: Steel
desc: Iron alloyed with a controlled amount of carbon for strength and toughness.

name: Glass
desc: An amorphous solid made by melting sand with soda and lime.

name: Writing
desc: Recording language with marks, beginning with Sumerian cuneiform and Egyptian hieroglyphs.

name: Numeral systems
desc: Symbols for recording quantities, grown out of clay counting tokens.

name: Alphabet
desc: A small set of letters standing for individual sounds.

name: Calendar
desc: A system for organizing days into months and years by sun and moon.

name: Coinage
desc: Standardized stamped metal pieces used as money.

name: Papyrus
desc: A writing surface made from pressed papyrus reed pith.

name: Paper
desc: Sheets of pressed plant fiber pulp, first made in Han China.

name: Lever
desc: A rigid bar pivoting on a fulcrum to multiply force.

name: Pulley
desc: A wheel carrying a rope to change the direction and size of a force.

name: Screw
desc: An inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder, converting rotation to linear force.

name: Gear
desc: Toothed wheels that mesh to transmit torque and change speed.

name: Lathe
desc: A machine that spins a workpiece against a cutting tool.

name: Geometry
desc: The axiomatic study of shape and space, systematized by Euclid.

name: Lime mortar
desc: Burnt limestone mixed with sand and water to bind masonry.

name: Roman concrete
desc: Lime and volcanic ash concrete that built the Pantheon and harbors.

name: Portland cement
desc: The hydraulic cement behind nearly all modern concrete.

name: Water wheel
desc: A wheel turned by flowing water to drive mills and machinery.

name: Windmill
desc: A wind-driven mill for grinding grain and pumping water.

name: Movable type
desc: Reusable individual characters arranged to print text.

name: Printing press
desc: Gutenberg's press with cast metal type, enabling mass-produced books.

name: Gunpowder
desc: An explosive mixture of saltpeter, sulfur and charcoal discovered in Tang China.

name: Compass
desc: A magnetized needle that points north, transforming navigation.

name: Mechanical clock
desc: A weight-driven clock regulated by an escapement.

name: Lens
desc: Ground glass that focuses or spreads light by refraction.

name: Telescope
desc: An instrument that magnifies distant objects using lenses or mirrors.

name: Microscope
desc: An instrument that magnifies objects too small to see by eye.

name: Hindu–Arabic numerals
desc: Positional decimal notation with a symbol for zero.

name: Algebra
desc: Solving equations with symbols for unknowns, named after al-Khwarizmi's book.

name: Scientific method
desc: Systematic observation, hypothesis and experiment.

name: Calculus
desc: The mathematics of change, developed by Newton and Leibniz.

name: Newtonian mechanics
desc: Newton's laws of motion and gravitation.

name: Vacuum pump
desc: A device that removes gas from a sealed volume, first built by von Guericke.

name: Coal mining
desc: Extracting coal from the ground, the fuel of industrialization.

name: Coke smelting
desc: Baked coal that let Abraham Darby smelt iron without charcoal.

name: Steam engine
desc: Newcomen's atmospheric engine, the first practical machine to turn heat into work.

name: Watt steam engine
desc: James Watt's separate-condenser engine, which made steam power efficient.

name: Cylinder boring machine
desc: Wilkinson's machine for boring accurate cylinders in cast iron.

name: Machine tools
desc: Powered machines for precisely cutting and shaping metal.

name: Interchangeable parts
desc: Components made to tolerances so that any one fits any assembly.

name: Factory system
desc: Centralized, power-driven production with wage labor.

name: Thermodynamics
desc: The science of heat, work and energy, spurred by the steam engine.

name: Modern chemistry
desc: Lavoisier's quantitative chemistry of elements and compounds.

name: Distillation
desc: Separating liquids by boiling and condensing them.

name: Electric battery
desc: Volta's stack of zinc and copper discs, the first steady source of current.

name: Electrolysis
desc: Driving chemical reactions with electric current.

name: Electromagnetism
desc: Ørsted's discovery that currents create magnetic fields.

name: Electromagnet
desc: A coil of wire that becomes a magnet when current flows.

name: Electric motor
desc: A machine converting electrical energy to rotation.

name: Electric generator
desc: A machine converting rotation to electricity by induction, after Faraday.

name: Electrical telegraph
desc: Sending coded messages over wires, first commercialized by Cooke, Wheatstone and Morse.

name: Electromagnetic theory
desc: Maxwell's unification of electricity, magnetism and light.

name: Telephone
desc: Transmitting speech as electrical signals over wire.

name: Incandescent light bulb
desc: A glowing filament in a vacuum bulb; the first practical electric light.

name: Transformer
desc: A device that changes AC voltage via mutual induction.

name: Electrical grid
desc: Networks generating and delivering electricity to consumers.

name: Photography
desc: Recording images chemically on light-sensitive surfaces.

name: Camera obscura
desc: A darkened chamber where a pinhole projects an image of the outside.

name: Vulcanized rubber
desc: Curing rubber with sulfur so it stays elastic and durable.

name: Oil drilling
desc: Drilled wells that tapped petroleum at scale, starting in Pennsylvania.

name: Oil refining
desc: Separating crude oil into kerosene, gasoline and other products.

name: Bessemer process
desc: Blowing air through molten pig iron to make cheap steel in bulk.

name: Steam locomotive
desc: A steam engine on wheels pulling trains along rails.

name: Railway
desc: Public rail networks beginning with the Stockton and Darlington.

name: Steamship
desc: A ship propelled by steam engines rather than sail.

name: Internal combustion engine
desc: An engine burning fuel inside its cylinders, perfected by Otto and Diesel.

name: Automobile
desc: A self-propelled road vehicle, starting with Benz's Patent-Motorwagen.

name: Assembly line
desc: Moving work past stationed workers, as in Ford's Highland Park plant.

name: Aluminium smelting
desc: Electrolytic reduction of alumina that made aluminium cheap.

name: Airplane
desc: A powered, fixed-wing aircraft, first flown by the Wright brothers.

name: Aerodynamics
desc: The study of air in motion and forces on bodies within it.

name: Rocket
desc: A vehicle propelled by reaction mass, first as Chinese fire arrows.

name: Liquid-propellant rocket
desc: Rockets burning liquid fuel and oxidizer, first flown by Robert Goddard.

name: Jet engine
desc: A reaction engine that propels aircraft by a fast exhaust jet.

name: Gas turbine
desc: A continuous-combustion engine driving a turbine with hot gas.

name: Radio
desc: Communication by electromagnetic waves, pioneered by Marconi.

name: Cathode-ray tube
desc: A vacuum tube steering electron beams onto a phosphor screen.

name: Vacuum tube
desc: An evacuated tube controlling electron flow; the first amplifier and switch.

name: Television
desc: Transmitting moving images and sound to receivers.

name: Radar
desc: Detecting objects by reflected radio waves.

name: Quantum mechanics
desc: The physics of atoms and subatomic particles.

name: Semiconductor physics
desc: Materials whose conductivity can be engineered, explained by band theory.

name: Transistor
desc: A solid-state amplifier and switch invented at Bell Labs.

name: Photolithography
desc: Patterning microscopic features with light and photoresist.

name: Integrated circuit
desc: Many transistors fabricated together on one chip, by Kilby and Noyce.

name: Microprocessor
desc: A complete CPU on a single chip, beginning with the Intel 4004.

name: Punched card
desc: Cards encoding data as holes, from Jacquard looms to tabulators.

name: Boolean algebra
desc: George Boole's algebra of true and false, the logic of digital circuits.

name: Electronic computer
desc: Programmable machines computing with electronic circuits, such as ENIAC and Colossus.

name: Personal computer
desc: A computer cheap and small enough for one person to own.

name: Packet switching
desc: Splitting data into routed packets, the basis of computer networks.

name: Internet
desc: The global network of networks running TCP/IP.

name: World Wide Web
desc: Tim Berners-Lee's system of linked hypertext documents over the internet.

name: Hypertext
desc: Text containing links to other text.

name: Mobile phone
desc: A portable telephone working over a cellular radio network.

name: Lithium-ion battery
desc: A rechargeable battery shuttling lithium ions, commercialized by Sony.

name: Smartphone
desc: A pocket computer with a touchscreen and mobile internet.

name: Laser
desc: A source of coherent light by stimulated emission.

name: Nuclear fission
desc: The splitting of heavy nuclei, discovered by Hahn, Strassmann and Meitner.

name: Nuclear reactor
desc: A controlled fission chain reaction, first achieved in Chicago Pile-1.

name: Nuclear weapon
desc: Bombs releasing energy from fission or fusion.

name: Solar cell
desc: A semiconductor device converting light directly to electricity.

name: Synthetic plastic
desc: Bakelite, the first fully synthetic plastic.

name: Germ theory of disease
desc: The understanding that microorganisms cause many diseases.

name: Vaccination
desc: Jenner's smallpox vaccine, inducing immunity with a harmless agent.

name: General anesthesia
desc: Ether and chloroform made painless surgery possible.

name: Penicillin
desc: The first widely used antibiotic, discovered by Alexander Fleming.

name: X-ray imaging
desc: Imaging the body's interior with Röntgen's newly discovered rays.

name: DNA structure
desc: Watson, Crick, Franklin and Wilkins revealed the double helix.

name: X-ray crystallography
desc: Determining atomic structures from X-ray diffraction patterns.

name: Recombinant DNA
desc: Splicing DNA from different organisms, by Cohen and Boyer.

name: Polymerase chain reaction
desc: Kary Mullis's method for copying DNA millions of times.

name: DNA sequencing
desc: Reading the order of bases in DNA, starting with Sanger's method.

name: Haber–Bosch process
desc: Synthesizing ammonia from air, the basis of nitrogen fertilizer.

name: Mechanical refrigeration
desc: Cooling by compressing and evaporating a refrigerant.

name: Canning
desc: Preserving food by sealing it in airtight containers and heating.

name: Artificial intelligence
desc: Machines performing tasks that require intelligence, founded as a field at Dartmouth.

name: Artificial satellite
desc: An object placed in orbit, starting with Sputnik 1.
